Meet your teacher

Meet Anna Zhu

Anna is a pianist, nationally certified piano educator, and the founder of Fly to the Moon Piano & Music Studio. She holds a master's degree in Communication and Public Relations from Johns Hopkins University.

Her experience includes teaching children and adults across different ages, learning styles, and musical goals, including children on the autism spectrum and older adults living with dementia.

Patience, communication, trust, and an understanding of each student are at the heart of her teaching.

Anna continues her own advanced piano studies with Victoria Bogdashevskaya, former principal pianist of the Seattle Symphony. Her goal is to help each student feel heard, supported, challenged, and inspired while building a lasting connection with music.

The studio

A space to learn, create & grow

Centered around a grand piano, the studio offers a calm, welcoming, and focused environment where students can step away from everyday distractions and connect deeply with music.

Whether a student is playing a first note or preparing for an advanced performance, curiosity is encouraged, mistakes are part of learning, and every musical milestone deserves to be celebrated.

Happy learning · Meaningful progress

Music is more than notes.

Students learn best when they feel safe, curious, understood, and excited to return to the piano.

01 · JOY

Joy comes first

Music should be something students look forward to. Lessons encourage curiosity and creativity while gradually building technique and musicianship.

02 · INDIVIDUALITY

Every student is different

Some students learn by listening, some visually, and others through movement, stories, patterns, questions, or understanding why.

03 · TRUST

Communication is essential

Students are encouraged to say what they love, what feels difficult, and when they would like to try another way. Their ideas are part of learning.

04 · GROWTH

Little missions, big progress

Joyful learning still includes clear goals and small challenges that build curiosity, independence, consistency, and confidence.

Weekly Music Missions

A technique goal, listening activity, practice challenge, creative exercise, or musical discovery gives each student an achievable next step. The goal is not perfection; it is the confidence to keep moving forward.

Questions are welcome

Studio FAQ

A few practical details for students and families considering lessons.

How does tuition payment work?

Tuition is accepted via Zelle or cash and is due at the beginning of each month. Monthly tuition reserves the student's regular weekly lesson time.

What is the cancellation and make-up policy?

Please provide at least 24 hours' notice to cancel or reschedule. Eligible make-up lessons may be arranged based on teacher and studio availability.

Are recitals offered?

Yes. Studio recitals are offered twice each year so students can share their progress, build confidence, and celebrate music. Participation is encouraged but not required.

Do you prepare students for competitions and exams?

Yes. Preparation plans can be developed for competitions, auditions, RCM and ABRSM examinations, and other performance opportunities according to the student's level, timeline, and goals.

Are master lessons available?

For selected students seeking advanced development, opportunities for master lessons with university music professors or professional musicians may be available when appropriate.

What happens when the teacher is on vacation?

Planned studio vacations will generally be communicated at least one month in advance so families have time to plan.

Can parents ask about progress or practice?

Absolutely. Questions about practice, repertoire, progress, motivation, scheduling, and lesson goals are always welcome. Communication between students, families, and the teacher is part of the learning process.
